# Lua API reference

<!-- Generated by tools/luagen.py from engine/api.xml; do not edit. -->

The shared sprite engine seen from Lua. Every module is a global table; value types (vec2, rect, color, purse, camera, text style, input) are Lua tables with a metatable, so `r:cut_top(66)` and `a + b` work and `{x = 1, y = 2}` is a valid vec2 - as in C, zero is the default for every field left out. Stateful objects (a city, a save file being read) are userdata handles with methods. Functions keep the names and the argument order of engine.h, minus their type prefix.

Argument types: `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `string`, the value types below, `T[]` for a sequence. A `?` marks an optional argument. Functions whose first argument is the module's own type are also methods: `rect.inflate(r, 4)` is `r:inflate(4)`.

## Modules

- [`num`](#num) - Scalar helpers the engine uses everywhere; `math` has the rest.
- [`vec2`](#vec2) - Constructor `vec2(x, y)`; operators + - * (by a number or component-wise) and unary minus; every function is also a method.
- [`size2`](#size2) - Constructor `size2(w, h)`.
- [`rect`](#rect) - Constructor `rect(x, y, w, h)`. Layout is RectCut: `rect.cut_top(r, 66)` slices 66 units off the top of r (changing r) and returns the slice.
- [`color`](#color) - Constructor `color(r, g, b, a)`; `color.hex(0xRRGGBB)`; constants WHITE, BLACK, CLEAR.
- [`purse`](#purse) - Constructor `purse(a, b, ...)`; operators + and -.
- [`app`](#app) - The window, the logical screen and the main loop. A game's main.lua returns the descriptor engine.h calls app_desc - `return {title = ..., id = ..., design = size2(1200, 900), max_aspect = 16 / 9, landscape = true, fixed = false, rotate_text = ..., clear = color.hex(0x0E2B2E), init = function() end, frame = function(dt) end, quit = function() end}` - and the engine runs it (fixed keeps the design size and letterboxes the rest; a fixed game with a max_aspect still grows along its long side up to that ratio, so read app.screen() for its height): init once the window exists, frame every frame, quit at the end. Command line options understood by every game: --size WxH, --fresh (no saves), --data DIR, --lua DIR, --shot out.png [--frames N].
- [`input`](#input)
- [`texture`](#texture)
- [`gfx`](#gfx) - Shapes and images, in logical screen units, drawn in call order.
- [`camera`](#camera)
- [`fx`](#fx) - Pooled particles and floating text in screen space.
- [`font`](#font)
- [`style`](#style) - Constructor `style{...}`; the methods return a tweaked copy.
- [`text`](#text) - Styled TrueType text. Every function returns the rect it drew.
- [`haptic`](#haptic) - Optional tactile feedback, independent of sound and reduced motion. Requests coalesce to the highest-priority effect each frame, with rate limiting for cascades; suppressed events are dropped. Native iOS and macOS, browser vibration when supported, otherwise silent. Headless, capture, smoke and test runs never drive hardware; --no-haptics also suppresses output.
- [`sfx`](#sfx) - A tiny synthesiser for feedback tones.
- [`ui`](#ui) - Native widgets plus shared Lua form resources. ui.form(template) provides layout, skins and model bindings; ui.modals(skin) owns nested modal layers. See docs/UI_ENGINE.md. Immediate widgets remain available: if ui.button(r, 'Play') then.
- [`sprite`](#sprite) - Authored atlas frames, pivot-aware bounds and animation timing.
- [`nav`](#nav) - nav.new(); assign nodes and live blockers, then find. Indices are 0-based.
- [`save`](#save)
- [`story`](#story) - Characters, dialogue and speech bubbles.
- [`city`](#city) - `city.new()` makes one; configure its fields, then `c:init(ground)`.

## purse

Constructor `purse(a, b, ...)`; operators + and -.

An amount of each resource: a sequence of up to purse.MAX integers (missing ones are 0). The game names the slots: `local COINS, INFLUENCE = 1, 2`.

- `purse.MAX` (integer) Resource slots in a purse.

## app

The window, the logical screen and the main loop. A game's main.lua returns the descriptor engine.h calls app_desc - `return {title = ..., id = ..., design = size2(1200, 900), max_aspect = 16 / 9, landscape = true, fixed = false, rotate_text = ..., clear = color.hex(0x0E2B2E), init = function() end, frame = function(dt) end, quit = function() end}` - and the engine runs it (fixed keeps the design size and letterboxes the rest; a fixed game with a max_aspect still grows along its long side up to that ratio, so read app.screen() for its height): init once the window exists, frame every frame, quit at the end. Command line options understood by every game: --size WxH, --fresh (no saves), --data DIR, --lua DIR, --shot out.png [--frames N].

### `app.quit()`

End the main loop after this frame.

### `app.screen()`

The logical screen, origin (0, 0).

**Returns:** `rect`

### `app.bleed()`

The whole display in logical units: the screen plus letterbox bars and safe-area margins (x and y may be negative). Draw backgrounds over it inside gfx.bleed(true); keep controls in app.screen().

**Returns:** `rect`

### `app.pixel_scale()`

Device pixels per logical unit.

**Returns:** `number`

### `app.time()`

Seconds since start (frame time).

**Returns:** `number`

### `app.dt()`

Duration of the current frame, seconds.

**Returns:** `number`

### `app.clock()`

## input

A snapshot of the pointer (mouse or first finger) with gestures. `input{pos = p, pinch = 1}` is an idle pointer at p.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `pos` | `vec2` | Pointer position, logical units. |
| `press_pos` | `vec2` | Where the current or last press started. |
| `down` | `boolean` | Held. |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | Went down this frame. |
| `released` | `boolean` | Went up this frame. |
| `tap` | `boolean` | Released this frame without dragging or multi-touch. |
| `dragging` | `boolean` | Moved further than the drag threshold. |
| `drag` | `vec2` | Movement this frame while dragging. |
| `captured` | `boolean` | The press started on UI; the world should ignore it. |
| `hover` | `boolean` | A real mouse is over the window. |
| `multi_touch` | `boolean` | A second pointer joined this press; latched through release, cleared on the next press or cancellation. |
| `wheel` | `number` | Wheel steps this frame. |
| `pinch` | `number` | Zoom factor from two fingers this frame (1 = none). |
| `pinch_center` | `vec2` |  |
| `key` | `integer` | AX key code pressed this frame, 0 if none. |
| `back` | `boolean` | Escape or the Android back button. |

- `input.KEY_SPACE` (integer)

- `input.KEY_TAB` (integer)

- `input.KEY_RETURN` (integer)

## haptic

Optional tactile feedback, independent of sound and reduced motion. Requests coalesce to the highest-priority effect each frame, with rate limiting for cascades; suppressed events are dropped. Native iOS and macOS, browser vibration when supported, otherwise silent. Headless, capture, smoke and test runs never drive hardware; --no-haptics also suppresses output.

- `haptic.TICK` (integer) Very light trickle/landing tick.

- `haptic.MATCH` (integer) Matched pieces or a hidden-object find.

- `haptic.COMBO` (integer) Cascade, special activation or chained finds.

- `haptic.PLACE` (integer) Committed building placement or relocation, or completed construction.

- `haptic.COLLECT` (integer) Resource collection.

- `haptic.SUCCESS` (integer) Level completion or rescue; highest priority.

- `haptic.ERROR` (integer) Rejected swap or hidden-object miss.

### `haptic.play(effect, strength?)`

Request a semantic one-shot effect, with strength clamped to [0,1] (default 1). Zero/nonfinite strength and unknown effects are ignored. Success/error use native notification patterns; macOS ignores strength. Call from gameplay events, never from drawing or speculative rules.

| Argument | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `effect` | `integer` |  |
| `strength` | `number?` | Default 1. |

### `haptic.enable(on)`

Enable independently of sfx; disabling drops pending feedback. Defaults on at app start.

| Argument | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `on` | `boolean` |  |

### `haptic.enabled()`

**Returns:** `boolean`

### `haptic.available()`

Whether the backend supports requests (iOS checks hardware). macOS trackpad and browser hardware/policy may still decline. Independent of enabled.

**Returns:** `boolean`

## city

`city.new()` makes one; configure its fields, then `c:init(ground)`.

The building meta-game: ground, zones, a catalogue of building types and the placed buildings. Fields read and write the engine's state; struct-valued fields are copied, so `local cam = c.cam; cam.view = r; c.cam = cam`. Callbacks receive the city as their first argument.

| Field | Type | Access | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ground` | `texture` | read | Loaded by init. |
| `defs` | `building_def[]` | read/write | The building catalogue; assign a sequence. |
| `items` | `building[]` | read/write | The placed buildings. |
| `count` | `integer` | read/write | How many buildings are placed. |
| `zones` | `city_zone[]` | read/write |  |
| `zone_count` | `integer` | read |  |
| `open` | `integer` | read/write | Bit per opened zone (bit 0 = zone 0, which starts open). |
| `spacing` | `number` | read/write | Minimum distance between buildings without footprints. |
| `tile` | `number` | read/write | A tile's side on the ground in world units; defaults to 45. Set it before init: building sizes are in tiles, projected by the engine's city camera. |
| `clearance` | `size2` | read/write | Tiles added to every sized footprint (w, h), so bases keep apart: size2(1, 1) leaves half a tile of ground on each side. Sprites keep their size. |
| `buildable` | `function` | read/write | function(c, world) -> bool: terrain test. |
| `zone_at` | `function` | read/write | function(c, world) -> zone (0-based) or -1; default: zone rects. |
| `zone_touches` | `function` | read/write | function(c, zone, open) -> bool: adjacency; default: rects touching. |
| `draw_over` | `function` | read/write | function(c): game drawing above the fog and buildings, below the ghost. |
| `cam` | `camera` | read/write |  |
| `fog` | `color` | read/write | Locked zones; default dark teal. |
| `fog_on_land_only` | `boolean` | read/write |  |
| `fog_clouds` | `boolean` | read/write | Animated world-space cloud density and billow lighting, clipped to the closed-region mask. |
| `path` | `color` | read/write | Paths linking buildings; alpha 0 = none. |
| `movable` | `boolean` | read/write | Hold a building still for 0.5 seconds to pick it up; ordinary drags pan the map. |
| `show_footprints` | `boolean` | read/write | Debug: draw every building's footprint and pivot over its sprite, to check the sprite's measurements. |
| `income_icon` | `texture` | read/write |  |
| `selected` | `integer` | read/write | Quick build: a tap places this type at once (-1 = off). |
| `placing` | `integer` | read | Building type being placed, -1 = none. |
| `moving` | `integer` | read | Index being moved, -1 = a new building. |
| `ghost` | `vec2` | read/write | Where it would go. |
| `held` | `boolean` | read/write | The ghost is being dragged: lifted over the footprint of the tile it will land on. |

**city.{NONE, BUILT, MOVED, BLOCKED, CANT_AFFORD, LOCKED_TYPE, COLLECTED, NOT_READY, PICKED, ZONE}** - city_event results.

| Value | |
|---|---|
| `city.BUILT` | A new building was placed and paid for. |
| `city.BLOCKED` | The spot is not free, not land or not open. |
| `city.LOCKED_TYPE` | The building's needs are not met. |
| `city.COLLECTED` | Income collected. |
| `city.PICKED` | Tapped a building without income. |
| `city.ZONE` | Tapped land in a closed zone (event.zone). |

- `city.MAX` (integer)

- `city.ZONES` (integer)

### building_def

A building type.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |

| `sprite_path` | `string` |  |
| `sprite` | `texture` | Loaded by city:init from sprite_path. |
| `shadow_path` | `string` | Optional separate ground-shadow image; with its own crop and pivot. |
| `shadow` | `texture` | Loaded by city:init from shadow_path; drawn beneath all buildings and stays grounded during lift animations. |
| `shadow_pivot` | `vec2` | Ground centre in shadow-image pixels; zero defaults to the sprite pivot for matching canvases. |
| `shadow_base_width` | `number` | Footprint's width in shadow-image pixels, so a low-resolution layer stays registered; zero uses the sprite's pixel scale. |
| `size` | `size2` | Footprint in whole tiles: w along the front-left side, h along the front-right; zero = a circle of city.spacing. |
| `pivot` | `vec2` | Sprite pixel of the footprint's ground centre, where the building stands; zero = bottom centre. |
| `base_width` | `number` | Sprite pixels from the footprint's left corner to its right one; sets the drawing scale. |
| `height` | `number` | Drawn height in world units; derived from base_width and size when both are set. |
| `cost` | `purse` | Paid when placed. |
| `reward` | `purse` | Granted once when placed. |
| `needs` | `purse` | Must be owned (not spent) to build. |
| `income` | `purse` | Collected by tapping when ready. |

| `screen` | `vec2` | Where it happened. |


## Shared Lua forms

The embedded UI framework extends ui with ui.form(template) and ui.modals(skin). See [UI engine resources, bindings, skins and modal layers](UI_ENGINE.md).

## Motion: ease and tween

The embedded motion module (engine/tween.lua) defines the easing catalogue `ease` and the tween, timeline, stagger, punch and shake API `tween`. See [Motion](MOTION.md).
